title: California's last-resort insurance pool expanded sharply in policies and insured exposure
source_unit: California FAIR Plan Association total policies in force and total insured exposure
geography: California; residential, commercial, and business-owner lines in the five-year county reports, with current quarterly total

observations.period: September 30 fiscal year ends, 2021-2025; total policies in force

denominator.unit: California FAIR Plan policies in force across residential, commercial, and business-owner lines

observations.method: Extraction from the FAIR Plan five-year county report; total row covers residential, commercial, and business-owner lines and uses fiscal-year-end stocks.
observations.uncertainty: Policy growth is not a direct count of households denied private insurance; lines of business are combined, policies may reflect changing coverage or insurer mix, and the series does not identify duplicate, replacement, or voluntarily selected policies.
observations.subgroup: California FAIR Plan total across the published lines of business; county-level detail is available in the source PDF.
observations.counterinterpretation: A growing residual pool can reflect new risk, prices, underwriting changes, policy changes, or transparency/reporting changes; it does not by itself prove private-market withdrawal or household displacement.

observations.period: September 30 fiscal year ends, 2021-2025; total insured exposure

denominator.unit: California FAIR Plan total insured exposure across published lines

observations.method: Extraction from the FAIR Plan five-year county report total row; exposure is the published total insured value measure, not realized loss.
observations.uncertainty: Exposure is a limit or insured-value stock, not an expected loss, claim payment, replacement cost, or household wealth measure; changes may reflect policy mix, limits, valuation, and line-of-business composition.
observations.subgroup: California FAIR Plan total across residential, commercial, and business-owner lines.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exposure can grow faster than policy count if higher-value properties enter the pool; it should not be read as equivalent to policyholder burden or state fiscal loss.

observations.period: June 2026; current quarterly FAIR Plan headline

denominator.unit: California FAIR Plan total dwelling and commercial policies/exposure headline

policy_change_from_september_2022.unit: percent increase in total policies in force

observations.method: Extraction from the FAIR Plan quarterly key-statistics page, current through June 2026; scope differs slightly in the page headline from the five-year fiscal-year report labels.
observations.uncertainty: The current page is a later point-in-time update, not a continuous annual panel; headline scope, fiscal timing, and line-of-business definitions must be checked before calculating a precise long-run rate.
observations.subgroup: California FAIR Plan total dwelling and commercial headline; detailed category PDFs are separate.
observations.counterinterpretation: A larger FAIR Plan pool can be a designed public backstop response and does not alone identify whether coverage is more or less affordable, adequate, or available in the voluntary market.

related_sources.claim: California Department of Insurance describes state distress-area and voluntary-market exposure metrics and FAIR Plan transparency requirements.
related_sources.access_boundary: State distress metrics are not equivalent to FAIR Plan enrollment or private-market denial.

related_sources.claim: Local archive preserves the current FAIR Plan headline page used for the June 2026 point.
related_sources.access_boundary: The archive captures the page text and linked source references, not every linked chart image.

boundary: This record establishes rapid growth in California's residual-market policy count and insured exposure, plus a current premium/exposure headline. It does not establish private-market nonrenewal causation, individual affordability, claims adequacy, repairs, household mobility, or political response.
